title: Box model, box-sizing and units (px, rem, em, %, vw/vh)

videos.script: Open DevTools on any page and hover over an element. {{hover}} A coloured rectangle lights up. Blue in the middle, green around it, a thin line, and orange outside. That picture is the most important diagram in CSS. {{box}} Every element on the page is a box. In the middle is its content: the text, the picture. Around that, padding, the space inside the edge. Then the border, the edge itself. Then margin, the space it keeps from its neighbours. {{width}} Here is the first surprise. You write width: three hundred pixels, and the card comes out three hundred and forty-eight. The padding and the border were added on top. One line of CSS changes that rule, and almost every site uses it. {{collapse}} The second surprise is margins. Two boxes, each with twenty-four pixels of margin, sit twenty-four pixels apart, not forty-eight. You will measure why. {{units}} Then the units. Pixels, which are not the pixels of your screen. Rem and em, which follow the text size. Percentages, which are a share of something, and you need to know of what. And the units that measure the window itself. {{end}} By the end, you can look at a box and say where every pixel of it came from. {{close}}
